title: Zeylenone Attenuates Tamoxifen Resistance by Directly Binding to CTCF and Inhibiting the CTCF-CENPK-JAK1/STAT3 Signaling Axis in Breast Cancer.
authors: Li, Gang; Deng, Zhiping; Zhang, Wenqing; Ge, Peng; Wang, Kai
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过分子对接和ChIP-qPCR等实验揭示Zeylenone直接结合CTCF并抑制其调控CENPK转录，涉及TF-DNA互作但以湿实验为主，AI/物理模拟方法仅初步应用，深度有限。
abstract: This study was designed to investigate the effects of zeylonone (Zey) on attenuating tamoxifen (TAM) resistance in breast cancer cells in vitro and in vivo and its underlying mechanisms. Database analysis and clinical sample validation revealed that CENPK is significantly upregulated in breast cancer tissues and TAM-resistant cells, and its expression positively correlates with CTCF mRNA levels. Knockdown of CENPK markedly suppressed proliferation and colony formation, induced G0/G1 cell cycle arrest, promoted apoptosis in MCF-7/TAM cells, and inhibited tumor growth in nude mice, thereby attenuating TAM resistance. Zey treatment resulted in dose- and time-dependent downregulation of both CTCF and CENPK at the protein and mRNA levels. Molecular docking provided preliminary computational evidence suggesting Zey can bind to CTCF (binding energy:-6.9 kcal/mol), with subsequent biophysical and functional assays supporting this interaction, and thermal shift assays demonstrated that Zey enhances the thermal stability of CTCF. ChIP-qPCR and luciferase reporter assays confirmed that CTCF directly binds to the CENPK promoter and positively regulates its transcription, and Zey inhibits this regulatory process by directly binding to CTCF. Mechanistically, the CTCF/CENPK axis is associated with JAK1/STAT3 pathway modulation (increasing phosphorylation levels of JAK1 and STAT3), and Zey significantly reduces pathway activity by suppressing this axis. Overexpression of CTCF attenuated the anti-resistance effects of Zey, whereas knockdown of CENPK or JAK1 restored Zey's efficacy. While CTCF and CENPK have been individually implicated in cancer progression, this study provides the first evidence linking them in a functional regulatory axis that drives tamoxifen resistance. Zey attenuates tamoxifen resistance in breast cancer cells by directly binding to CTCF, thereby inhibiting CTCF-mediated transcriptional regulation of CENPK, downregulating CENPK expression, and subsequently suppressing the JAK1/STAT3 signaling pathway.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在探讨zeylonone（Zey）在体外和体内对乳腺癌细胞他莫昔芬（TAM）耐药的缓解作用及其潜在机制。数据库分析和临床样本验证显示，CENPK在乳腺癌组织和TAM耐药细胞中显著上调，其表达与CTCF mRNA水平呈正相关。敲低CENPK显著抑制MCF-7/TAM细胞的增殖和集落形成，诱导G0/G1细胞周期阻滞，促进凋亡，并抑制裸鼠肿瘤生长，从而缓解TAM耐药。Zey处理在蛋白和mRNA水平上导致CTCF和CENPK呈剂量和时间依赖性下调。分子对接提供了初步计算证据，提示Zey可与CTCF结合（结合能：-6.9 kcal/mol），后续生物物理和功能实验支持这一相互作用，热位移实验表明Zey增强CTCF的热稳定性。ChIP-qPCR和荧光素酶报告基因实验证实，CTCF直接结合CENPK启动子并正向调控其转录，而Zey通过直接结合CTCF抑制这一调控过程。机制上，CTCF/CENPK轴与JAK1/STAT3通路调节相关（增加JAK1和STAT3的磷酸化水平），Zey通过抑制该轴显著降低通路活性。CTCF过表达减弱了Zey的抗耐药效应，而敲低CENPK或JAK1则恢复Zey的疗效。尽管CTCF和CENPK各自已被单独涉及癌症进展，本研究首次提供证据将它们联系在一个驱动他莫昔芬耐药的功能性调控轴中。Zey通过直接结合CTCF，抑制CTCF介导的CENPK转录调控，下调CENPK表达，并随后抑制JAK1/STAT3信号通路，从而缓解乳腺癌细胞的他莫昔芬耐药。
